correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<alpha<2, sigma,r>0, -1<lambda<1, stable scaling makes one physical reset excursion a small-time flight from lambda in (-1,1). The Lévy–Itô single-jump measure gives successful mass epsilon*a/r and marked density epsilon*e^(-rt)c|v-lambda|^(-1-alpha), with pre-jump position tending lambda. The proof splits large jumps at a fixed boundary-safe cutoff and bounds bounded-jump excursions by an exponential martingale; the boundary-strip contribution vanishes. Inserting this measure into the exact geometric renewal transform yields the joint Laplace limit a/(a+u) times the independent Exp(r) age and normalized exit mark. For the reset count, the stopped Poisson martingale has variance r E S_L=O(L^alpha), proving (R_L-rS_L)/L^alpha→0. Direct integration gives c and a_±, and centered |Y| tail z^(-alpha). The limit excludes alpha=2, varying lambda or r; no assertion of finite-L independence or error rate.
residual_risks: The delicate small-jump o(epsilon) probability follows an exponential martingale only after choosing cutoff relative to desired displacement; the proof spells out this order, but no complete independent martingale writeup reproduced.
